label: text
text: Reports indicate that pilferage at Havre is again on the increase. Theft occurs more frequently in the case of valuable imports, and only quite recently a loss of 10 per cent. of the entire value of a consignment occurred. Imports from India are extensively pilfered.

label: text
text: At Emden, Germany, during the fishing season of 1924 herring fishermen tried out airplanes to aid in the locating of schools of herring at sea, but the results were distinctly disappointing. Equipped with radio apparatus to report back to their base the air pilots cruised over the water looking for signs of the fish, but it was found that the airplanes move too fast, and the herring swim too far beneath the surface of the sea, for the observers to detect them.

label: text
text: Once more an English season of plays is being given in Paris. This time it is a Shaw cycle: It is curious that almost any well-organized theatrical enterprise in English is certain to succeed in the French capital. Not that the French themselves attend in large numbers; they are only mildly interested, although their theatrical papers give considerable space to these events. But the British and American colonies in Paris are so large in themselves that they can well support any theatre which offers them what they want. At this moment Shaw appears to be what they want. They have had an opportunity of witnessing many more of his plays than could be easily seen, if at all, in a limited space of time anywhere in America or in England.

label: text
text: A London journalist writes:—I remember a Glasgow Labour leader telling me that if the King and Queen were to walk through the Clydeside slums they would have such a welcome as would defen them—"and," he added grimly, "we would like to hang one or two other people—an insurance agent, a factor, and if possible a landlord; afterwards, just to round off a perfect day."

label: text
text: The annual report of the British Army for the year ending September 30 last gives the total strength of the regular army, all ranks as 215,343, with territorial reserve forces of 417,089. Enlistments and re-enlistments during the year totalled 30,000, or 878 less than for the previous year. Emigration to the Dominions is said to have proved a serious counter-attraction to army life, and many recruits have been lost in consequence.

label: text
text: Meudon, a little town in the Paris suburbs, noted for its beautiful woods, has just had a curious strike. There was an election for the Municipal Council, but there were no candidates and no electors. Such unanimity is rarely seen. Nobody broke the tacit understanding of abstaining from the polls. The reason is that it was proposed by Paris, against the wish of the inhabitants, to impose upon them an installation they did not desire. Thereupon the Council resigned in protest, and the townsfolk unanimously abstained from voting. What is more, Meudon has by these tactics managed to win its way, and the objectionable proposal is withdrawn. It is now to be presumed that candidates will present themselves for the Municipal Council and that the inhabitants will vote for them.

label: text
text: Proposals that the Shanghai Municipal Council donate Tls. 10,000 toward the construction of the proposed new building for the Y.M.C.A. were rejected at a recent meeting of the Finance Committee of the Council. The committee took the stand that in view of the Council's policy with regard to contributions to institutions which benefit one section of the community only, and also the fact that if this application be granted other institutions will expect similar treatment, the matter should be referred by a private citizen to the ratepayers for their approval.

label: text
text: It was announced at the meeting of the General Committee of the Church Missionary Society on February 17 that the Board of Governors of the West China Union University (in which the society co-operates) had recently admitted women students to the University; and the opinion was expressed that this was a significant sign showing that the remote inland provinces were coming into line with the more advanced coast provinces in offering educational facilities to women.

label: text
text: The latest service which the everactive Salvation Army has instituted is a "Darby and Jon" home for aged couple who have no means beyond the old-age pension and are without friends to help them. The first of these homes is in the village of Southborough, near Tunbridge Wells. Here in a house, formerly a girls' school, accommodation is provided for fourteen couples. Each couple has a large room with the necessary furniture, and each pair is allowed to bring such pictures and odds and ends, which may include a favourite armchair, as will give the place a "homey" look. In the large dining room separate tables sent two couples and four good substantial meals are provided daily. There is a large garden, in which the inmates of the home may work if they choose.

label: text
text: The Prince of Wales delights in these world tours of his. He takes the ceremonial side very flight-heartedly, and he has long since got over being fretted by the thought of having to prepare or deliver speeches. It is all in the day's work for him, and nothing tires him. He loves being in a state of perpetual motion, with new things to see and new people to meet.

label: text
text: It will come as a surprise to most people to learn that Charlie Chaplin's famous "duckshuffle," which has probably made him what he is today, is copied from a London cabby. Charlie said that the trousers, bowler, and willow cane were his own devices and that no one had ever worn such a costume before he first appeared in them on the American screen.

label: text
text: The Vicar of St. Andrew's, Kowloon, in his monthly letter says:—Good Friday cannot be a holiday. It is not a day either for tea dansants, or for staying at home moping. Some may have intended to give the day to golf or another game, or, to do "nothing in particular." There are some who could go to a dance on the anniversary of their mother's death. Happily, such people are rare. Even the most indifferent have, at times at least, a sense of congruity, and, surely, no one with any sense of the fitness of things can do otherwise than observe this day. How one should do so must be left to the individual conscience. Will you who read this letter think about it?

text: Mr. R. D. Manfield, Acting Commissioner of Customs at Chunking died on Friday, March 6, at 3 p.m. He had been ill but three days, but the severe attack of pneumonia was too much for his already weak heart. Mr. Manfield has been in Chunking only since December 24, 1924.

text: A silver cigarette case was presented to Colonel C. F. Grantham, of Surrey, at the annuas conference of the south-eastern area of the British Legion—at which he was re-elected chairman of the branch for the coming year—in recognition of his work for the Legion. He said his family had many heirlooms, one of which—General Wolfe's ring—he was wearing. None of those heirlooms would, however, be more valued than that gift from ex-Service men.
